feature1.prompt: Implement enhancements and modifications to the existing ITRS transformation logic. This feature focuses on improving how transformations within the ITRS framework handle coordinates, particularly by treating ITRS positions as time invariant and having the output frame adopt its own obstime. The changes update existing methods to use the observer’s location rather than a fixed Earth center, thereby refining the conversion between ITRS and related frames such as TETE and CIRS. This adjustment is designed to address recurring issues with inaccurate ITRS to AltAz transforms and to clarify the distinction between geocentric and topocentric aberration.
feature1.hint_texts: Focus on modifying the files astropy/coordinates/builtin_frames/intermediate_rotation_transforms.py and astropy/coordinates/builtin_frames/itrs.py. Update functions such as tete_to_itrs, itrs_to_tete, cirs_to_itrs, and itrs_to_cirs to incorporate the observer’s location and ensure that the obstime of the output frame is adopted. Add and manage the EarthLocationAttribute in the ITRS class, and update related transform graph registrations so that all transformations continue to work correctly with the new location handling.
feature1.entrypoint: Files to modify: astropy/coordinates/builtin_frames/intermediate_rotation_transforms.py and astropy/coordinates/builtin_frames/itrs.py. Key functions include tete_to_itrs, itrs_to_tete, cirs_to_itrs, and itrs_to_cirs; in itrs.py, integrate the EarthLocationAttribute alongside TimeAttribute. Developers should start their work around the code blocks near line 70 in intermediate_rotation_transforms.py and line 3 in itrs.py where the attributes and transform functions are defined.

feature2.prompt: Introduce new transformation logic for direct ITRS to Observed frame conversions. This feature implements a direct approach that converts ITRS coordinates to observed frames (AltAz and HADec) entirely within the ITRS framework, bypassing the complexities of geocentric versus topocentric aberration. The new methods treat ITRS positions as time invariant by adopting the output frame's obstime and accurately applying refraction corrections when necessary. This streamlined approach is intended to resolve persistent issues with the inaccuracy of ITRS to AltAz transformations and to simplify the conversion process for observers.
feature2.hint_texts: Develop a new file named astropy/coordinates/builtin_frames/itrs_observed_transforms.py to encapsulate the direct ITRS to Observed transformation logic. Implement functions such as itrs_to_observed and observed_to_itrs, and create supporting routines (e.g., itrs_to_altaz_mat, itrs_to_hadec_mat, add_refraction, and remove_refraction) for matrix operations and refraction correction. Ensure that the new transformation functions correctly handle both AltAz and HADec frames and interact with the updated ITRS attributes introduced in Feature1.
feature2.entrypoint: File to add: astropy/coordinates/builtin_frames/itrs_observed_transforms.py. Key functions to implement include itrs_to_observed and observed_to_itrs, as well as helper functions itrs_to_altaz_mat, itrs_to_hadec_mat, add_refraction, and remove_refraction. Developers should begin by outlining the transformation matrices and refraction correction logic as described in the problem statement.

tests.PASS_TO_PASS: No additional legacy tests; these new tests are designed to validate the direct observed transformation logic and refraction handling.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features interact with the ITRS frame’s core attributes, including the TimeAttribute and the new EarthLocationAttribute, as well as the coordinate transformation graph infrastructure used in astropy.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature1 must ensure the updated ITRS transformations correctly incorporate observer location and time invariance, which Feature2 will then leverage when converting directly to observed frames. The two teams should align on how the ITRS frame stores and propagates location and obstime data to guarantee seamless integration between legacy and new transformation logic.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers working on each feature should coordinate on the treatment of obstime and location data in the ITRS frame. Regular discussions and integration reviews are essential to ensure that the modifications in Feature1 do not conflict with the new transformation routines in Feature2, and that both parts work cohesively for a complete solution.
